title: Canonical minimal models in numerical dimension one
exact_target: If a smooth connected projective complex n-fold, $n\geq 3$, has pseudo-effective $K_X$ with Nakayama numerical Kodaira dimension $\kappa _\sigma (K_X)=1$, must a finite sequence of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips reach a projective Q-factorial terminal model Y with nef $K_Y$? On a common resolution must $p*K_X=q*K_Y+E$ hold with E effective q-exceptional and containing every contracted X-prime in its support?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
If a smooth connected projective complex n-fold, $n\geq 3$, has pseudo-effective $K_X$ with Nakayama numerical Kodaira dimension $\kappa _\sigma (K_X)=1$, must a finite sequence of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips reach a projective Q-factorial terminal model Y with nef $K_Y$? On a common resolution must $p*K_X=q*K_Y+E$ hold with E effective q-exceptional and containing every contracted X-prime in its support?

\subsection{Short English statement}
If a smooth connected projective complex n-fold, $n\geq 3$, has pseudo-effective $K_X$ with Nakayama numerical Kodaira dimension $\kappa _\sigma (K_X)=1$, must a finite sequence of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips reach a projective Q-factorial terminal model Y with nef $K_Y$? On a common resolution must $p*K_X=q*K_Y+E$ hold with E effective q-exceptional and containing every contracted X-prime in its support?
